text: screen="SIS" performs one marginal screen. screen="ISIS" repeats screening current model, incorporating predictions offsets, keeps best joint-fitting round. screen="auto" enables ISIS ultrahigh-dimensional designs. screen="none" fits supplied design directly. nsis controls SIS retained set ISIS batch. default ISIS batch GIC-based. small batch lets joint fitting remove false positives search progresses. code: set.seed(31) X <- matrix(rnorm(250*5000), 250, 5000) beta <- numeric(5000); beta[c(5, 50, 500)] <- c(2, -1.5, 1) y <- as.numeric(X %*% beta) + rnorm(250) fit <- L0glm.fit(X, y, family=gaussian(), lambda="gic",   screen="ISIS", screen.nthreads=2L, relaxed=TRUE) L0glm.metrics(fit, beta_true=beta)[c("gic", "TP", "FP", "FN", "TN", "F1_score", "MCC")] #>   gic TP FP FN   TN F1_score MCC #> 1 797  3  0  0 4997        1   1

1), y_ref_full, type = "l",        main = "FULL convolution", xlab = "time index", ylab = "signal")   lines(1:(n + L - 1), y_full, col = 2, lty = 3)             # identical      centre_shift <- (L + 1) / 2 - title: Information-criterion presets for sparse GLMs — information_criteria
text: single response, target information criterion form $$-2\ell(\widehat\beta) + \lambda k,$$ \(\ell\) log-likelihood \(k\) counts selected coefficients. presets set per-coefficient \(L_0\) penalty minus twice log-likelihood scale, rather \(-\ell\) mean-loss scale. logarithms natural. ordinary GLMs, \(n\) number rows X; special families use conventions model_criteria. \(p\) original number selectable predictors, excluding intercepts mandatory terms. preset resolved predictors removed, including screening explicit zero starts. pool selectable predictors uses \(p=1\) logarithms. Mandatory terms unpenalized coefficient updates; scoring counts parameter dimensions even fitted value zero, adding model-independent criterion term. "aic": Akaike information criterion \(\lambda = 2\). prediction-oriented choice based estimated expected Kullback–Leibler loss (Akaike, 1974). often retains variables generally consistent exact support recovery. "bic": Bayesian information criterion \(\lambda = \log n\). conventional choice identifying parsimonious model candidate dimension fixed moderate (Schwarz, 1978). classical consistency guarantee requires correctly specified identifiable model regularity conditions; need control overfitting large model spaces. "gic": generalized information criterion \(\lambda = \log p\,\log\log n\). selection-oriented choice sparse problems, including high-dimensional settings. Fan Tang (2013), Corollary 1, justify choice assumptions design, response tails, signal strength candidate model path. consistent choice conditions, uniquely optimal penalty every finite sample. "ebic": linearized extended BIC \(\lambda = \log n + 2\gamma_{\rm EBIC}\log p\), package default \(\gamma_{\rm EBIC}=\max\{0,1-\log n/(2\log p)\}\). accounts large model spaces (Chen Chen, 2008). implementation replaces combinatorial term \(2\gamma_{\rm EBIC}\log {p \choose k}\) \(2\gamma_{\rm EBIC}k\log p\), giving constant penalty per coefficient. default reduces BIC \(p\le\sqrt n\). Supply numeric lambda use different \(\gamma_{\rm EBIC}\); separate fitter's adaptive-ridge exponent gamma. "mbic": modified BIC \(\lambda = \log(np^2/16)\). multiplicity-adjusted criterion intended sparse selection among many candidate predictors (Bogdan, Ghosh Zak-Szatkowska, 2008). constant used follows Frommlet Nuel (2016). distinct false-discovery-rate-oriented mBIC2 criterion.

title: Fit generalized linear model with \(L_0\) or grouped row-\(L_0\) regularization subject to optional nonnegativity constraints — L0glm.fit
text: Tom Wenseleers, Laura Lanzas & Christophe Vanderaa Tom Wenseleers tom.wenseleers@kuleuven.\ Laboratory Socioecology Social Evolution, KU Leuven \ https://bio.kuleuven./eeb/tw/research \ ORCID: 0000-0002-1434-861X

title: Fit generalized linear model with \(L_0\) or grouped row-\(L_0\) regularization subject to optional nonnegativity constraints — L0glm.fit
code: # Single-channel Poisson deconvolution: shifted copies of a known PSF. single <- simul(method=2, n=500, p=500, s=.1, seed=2) fit_single <- L0glm.fit(single$X, single$y, family=poisson(identity),   lambda="gic", nonnegative=TRUE, relaxed=TRUE, parallelize=FALSE) L0glm.metrics(fit_single, beta_true=single$beta_true)[   c("gic", "TP", "FP", "FN", "TN", "F1_score", "MCC")]  old_par <- par(no.readonly=TRUE) par(mfrow=c(1, 1), mgp=c(2, .7, 0)) # The default PSF has peak one. Scale both spike trains by the same PSF peak # to display them in signal units; negative values indicate mirroring only. spike_scale <- max(single$X) beta_single <- as.numeric(coef(fit_single)) mu_single <- as.numeric(fitted(fit_single)) height <- max(as.numeric(single$y), as.numeric(single$y_true), mu_single,   as.numeric(single$beta_true)*spike_scale, beta_single*spike_scale) plot(single$x, single$y, type="l", col="grey65", ylim=c(-1, 1)*height*1.15,   xlab="Time", ylab="Signal / spike height (fit mirrored)",   main="Single-channel Poisson deconvolution") abline(h=0, col="grey75", lty=3) lines(single$x, single$y_true, col="grey30", lty=2) segments(single$x_beta, 0, single$x_beta,   as.numeric(single$beta_true)*spike_scale, col="navy") lines(single$x, -mu_single, col="orange", lwd=1.5) segments(single$x_beta, 0, single$x_beta, -beta_single*spike_scale, col="red") legend("topright", c("Observed signal", "True signal", "True spikes",   "Fitted signal (mirrored)", "Fitted spikes (mirrored)"),   col=c("grey65", "grey30", "navy", "orange", "red"),   lty=c(1, 2, 1, 1, 1), bty="n", cex=.75)  # Multichannel Poisson deconvolution: select rows shared across channels. # Retain every mass channel generated by the simulation. multi <- simul(method=4, n=500, p=500, s=.05, seed=2) fit_multi <- L0glm.fit(multi$X, multi$y, family=poisson(identity),   lambda="gic", nonnegative=TRUE, grouped=TRUE, relaxed=TRUE,   parallelize=FALSE) L0glm.metrics(fit_multi, beta_true=multi$beta_true)[   c("gic", "TP", "FP", "FN", "TN", "F1_score", "MCC",     "within_row_F1_score", "within_row_MCC")] # The within-row scores assess channel sparsity among correctly recovered rows. dim(coef(fit_multi))                  # original predictors by response channels par(mfrow=c(2, 1)) plotmat(multi$beta_true, xlab="Spike location", ylab="Channel",   main="True multichannel coefficients") plotmat(coef(fit_multi), xlab="Spike location", ylab="Channel",   main="Estimated multichannel coefficients") par(old_par)  # Precluster into at most 32 channel groups, select on their summed counts, # then refine and return coefficients for every original mass channel. system.time(fit_multi_clustered <- L0glm.fit(multi$X, multi$y,   family=poisson(identity), lambda="gic", nonnegative=TRUE,   grouped=TRUE, relaxed=TRUE, parallelize=TRUE, ncores=4L,   precluster=TRUE, cluster.refit=TRUE,   control.precluster=list(k.max=32L, rowbins=5L))) fit_multi_clustered$preclustering$clusters fit_multi_clustered$preclustering$seconds L0glm.metrics(fit_multi_clustered, beta_true=multi$beta_true)[   c("gic", "TP", "FP", "FN", "TN", "F1_score", "MCC",     "within_row_F1_score", "within_row_MCC")] dim(coef(fit_multi_clustered))         # all original predictors and channels  # A smooth nonnegative background: append a low-df spline basis and keep # those columns unpenalized. Poisson backgrounds add directly to the signal. B <- splines::bs(seq(0, 1, length.out=nrow(multi$X)), df=6, intercept=TRUE) alpha <- outer(c(2, 5, 3, 7, 4, 2), seq(.5, 1.5, length.out=ncol(multi$y))) set.seed(3) Y_background <- multi$y + matrix(rpois(length(multi$y), B %*% alpha),   nrow(multi$y), ncol(multi$y)) X_background <- cbind(multi$X, Matrix::Matrix(B, sparse=TRUE)) compulsory <- ncol(multi$X) + seq_len(ncol(B)) fit_background <- L0glm.fit(X_background, Y_background,   family=poisson(identity), lambda="gic", nonnegative=TRUE,   always.include=compulsory, grouped=TRUE, relaxed=TRUE,   precluster=TRUE, ncores=4L,   control.precluster=list(k.max=32L, rowbins=5L)) background_hat <- B %*% as.matrix(coef(fit_background)[compulsory, , drop=FALSE]) # Every original mass channel is retained in both the peak and background fit. dim(coef(fit_background)) fit_background$nuisance$seconds L0glm.metrics(fit_background,   beta_true=rbind(multi$beta_true, Matrix::Matrix(alpha, sparse=TRUE)))[   c("gic", "TP", "FP", "FN", "TN", "F1_score", "MCC",     "within_row_F1_score", "within_row_MCC")]  # High-dimensional Gaussian regression with positive and negative effects. # Run manually: the dense design alone occupies about 4 GB. if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ n <- 500L p <- 1000000L set.seed(123) X_hd <- matrix(rnorm(n*p), n, p) support <- sample.int(p, 60L) beta_hd <- numeric(p) beta_hd[support] <- runif(60L, -.8, .8) mean_hd <- as.numeric(X_hd[, support, drop=FALSE] %*% beta_hd[support]) set.seed(1) y_hd <- mean_hd + rnorm(n)  # screen="auto" activates ISIS exactly when p_eligible > 10*n. Screened fits # default to the original-p GIC preset and a relaxed refit. # Screening threads are independent of BLAS threads (nthreads). system.time(fit_hd <- L0glm.fit(X_hd, y_hd, screen.nthreads=8, nthreads=1)) fit_hd$screening[c("method", "screen_size", "iterations", "best_iteration", "nthreads")] fit_hd$screening$history L0glm.metrics(fit_hd, beta_true=beta_hd)[   c("gic", "TP", "FP", "FN", "TN", "F1_score", "MCC")] dim(coef(fit_hd))                    # all p rows, including screened-out zeros # Explicit alternatives: screen="SIS", "ISIS", or "none". } # }  # Basic controls: intercept constraints, dispersion and binomial fits. x <- seq(-1, 1, length.out=30) X <- matrix(x, ncol=1)  # Nonnegativity includes the Gaussian intercept. constrained <- L0glm.fit(X, -2+3*x, family=gaussian(),   intercept=TRUE, nonnegative=TRUE, lambda=1e-8,   dispersion=1, parallelize=FALSE) as.numeric(constrained$coefficients)  # Estimate Gaussian variance from an automatic or user-supplied start. set.seed(1) y_gaussian <- 2*x + rnorm(length(x), sd=.5) automatic <- L0glm.fit(X, y_gaussian, family=gaussian(),   lambda="gic", dispersion=NULL, maxit=100, parallelize=FALSE) initialized <- L0glm.fit(X, y_gaussian, family=gaussian(),   lambda="gic", dispersion=-.25, maxit=100, parallelize=FALSE) # dispersion=.25 instead keeps the variance fixed at .25.  # A binomial intercept may remain negative with a nonnegative slope. y <- round(1000*plogis(-2+x))/1000 logistic <- L0glm.fit(X, y, family=binomial(),   weights=rep(1000, length(y)), nonnegative=TRUE,   lambda=1e-8, parallelize=FALSE) as.numeric(logistic$coefficients)  # Gaussian validation-based stopping: keep a separate test set for assessment. set.seed(42) X_validation <- matrix(rnorm(200*40), 200, 40) y_validation <- 3 + 2*X_validation[, 1] - X_validation[, 2] + rnorm(200) train <- 1:120 fit_stopped <- L0glm.fit(X_validation[train, ], y_validation[train],   intercept=TRUE, lambda="gic", relaxed=TRUE, maxit=100,   validation=list(X=X_validation[-train, ], y=y_validation[-train]),   parallelize=FALSE) fit_stopped$validation$selection[c("best_iteration", "iterations", "stopped")]  # Optionally select the ISIS batch on the same validation set. # Omit nsis to keep the GIC-based default batch. fit_batch <- L0glm.fit(X_validation[train, ], y_validation[train],   intercept=TRUE, lambda="gic", screen="ISIS", nsis=c(1, 3, 5, 10),   relaxed=TRUE, maxit=100, validation=list(     X=X_validation[-train, ], y=y_validation[-train], rule="1se"),   parallelize=FALSE) fit_batch$validation[c("selected_start", "selected_nsis", "deviance")] fit_batch$validation$starts # Sparse special families: GIC preset fits, GIC tuning and three-fold CV. if (requireNamespace("mgcv", quietly=TRUE)) {   set.seed(204)   n <- 300L   X_special <- matrix(rnorm(n*20), n, 20)   folds_special <- sample(rep(1:3, length.out=n))   family_par <- par(mgp=c(2, .7, 0))    # Negative binomial: two nonzero slopes among 20 predictors.   mu_nb <- exp(.4 + .8*X_special[, 1] - .6*X_special[, 2])   y_nb <- rnbinom(n, mu=mu_nb, size=2)   # nb() estimates theta; nb(theta=2) would keep it fixed at two.   nb_fit <- L0glm.fit(X_special, y_nb, family=mgcv::nb(),     intercept=TRUE, lambda="gic", relaxed=TRUE, maxit=100, tol=1e-8)   nb_fit$theta   coef(nb_fit)   nb_gic <- L0glm.tune(X_special, y_nb, family=mgcv::nb(),     intercept=TRUE, tune="gic", nlambda=5,     relaxed=TRUE, maxit=100, tol=1e-8)   nb_cv <- L0glm.tune(X_special, y_nb, family=mgcv::nb(),     intercept=TRUE, tune="cv", nlambda=5, nfolds=3, foldid=folds_special,     relaxed=TRUE, maxit=100, tol=1e-8)   c(GIC=nb_gic$lambda_best, CV=nb_cv$lambda_best, CV_1se=nb_cv$lambda_1se)   predict(nb_cv$fit_1se, X_special[1:5, , drop=FALSE], type="response")    # Three-category multinomial: only two predictor rows affect probabilities.   eta <- cbind(0, .9*X_special[, 1] - .7*X_special[, 2],     -.8*X_special[, 1] + .6*X_special[, 2])   probabilities <- exp(eta - apply(eta, 1, max))   probabilities <- probabilities/rowSums(probabilities)   y_multinomial <- factor(vapply(seq_len(n), function(i)     sample.int(3, 1, prob=probabilities[i, ]), integer(1)), levels=1:3)   multinomial_fit <- L0glm.fit(X_special, y_multinomial,     family=mgcv::multinom(K=2), lambda="gic", grouped=TRUE,     relaxed=TRUE, maxit=200, tol=1e-8)   coef(multinomial_fit)               # original-scale, zero-sum CLR rows   multinomial_gic <- L0glm.tune(X_special, y_multinomial,     family=mgcv::multinom(K=2), tune="gic", nlambda=5, grouped=TRUE,     relaxed=TRUE, maxit=200, tol=1e-8)   multinomial_cv <- L0glm.tune(X_special, y_multinomial,     family=mgcv::multinom(K=2), tune="cv", nlambda=5,     nfolds=3, foldid=folds_special, grouped=TRUE,     relaxed=TRUE, maxit=200, tol=1e-8)   c(GIC=multinomial_gic$lambda_best, CV=multinomial_cv$lambda_best,     CV_1se=multinomial_cv$lambda_1se)   predict(multinomial_cv$fit_1se, X_special[1:5, , drop=FALSE], type="response")    # Right-censored Cox model: two nonzero log-hazard effects, no intercept.   if (requireNamespace("survival", quietly=TRUE)) {     event_time <- rexp(n, rate=exp(.7*X_special[, 1] - .5*X_special[, 2]))     censor_time <- rexp(n, rate=.4)     y_cox <- survival::Surv(pmin(event_time, censor_time),       event_time <= censor_time)     cox_fit <- L0glm.fit(X_special, y_cox, family=mgcv::cox.ph(),       lambda="gic", relaxed=TRUE, maxit=100, tol=1e-8)     coef(cox_fit)     cox_gic <- L0glm.tune(X_special, y_cox, family=mgcv::cox.ph(),       tune="gic", nlambda=5, relaxed=TRUE, maxit=100, tol=1e-8)     cox_cv <- L0glm.tune(X_special, y_cox, family=mgcv::cox.ph(),       tune="cv", nlambda=5, nfolds=3, foldid=folds_special,       relaxed=TRUE, maxit=100, tol=1e-8)     c(GIC=cox_gic$lambda_best, CV=cox_cv$lambda_best, CV_1se=cox_cv$lambda_1se)     predict(cox_cv$fit_1se, X_special[1:5, , drop=FALSE], type="risk")   }   par(family_par) }

code: # Small versions of the L0glm.fit deconvolution and Gaussian ISIS examples. # Five lambda values and three folds keep these examples short; increase # nlambda and nfolds for a finer search. True coefficients are only used # for plots and recovery metrics, never for fitting or choosing lambda. old_par <- par(mgp=c(2, .7, 0))  # Single-channel Poisson deconvolution. # Zoom around the GIC preset; use prop_range=1 for the full lambda range. single <- simul(method=2, n=500, p=500, s=.1, seed=2) single_gic <- L0glm.tune(single$X, single$y, family=poisson(identity),   tune="gic", nlambda=5, prop_range=.25, coefs.true=single$beta_true,   nonnegative=TRUE, relaxed=TRUE, parallelize=FALSE, plot=TRUE)  # Venetian-blind CV: train on two out of every three time points. folds <- rep(1:3, length.out=nrow(single$X)) single_cv <- L0glm.tune(single$X, single$y, family=poisson(identity),   tune="cv", nlambda=5, prop_range=.25, nfolds=3, foldid=folds,   coefs.true=single$beta_true,   nonnegative=TRUE, relaxed=TRUE, parallelize=FALSE, plot=TRUE) c(GIC=single_gic$lambda_best, CV=single_cv$lambda_best,   CV_1se=single_cv$lambda_1se, GIC_preset=single_cv$lambda_preset) single_cv$metrics[c("lambda", "cv_deviance", "cv_se")] L0glm.metrics(single_gic$fit_best, beta_true=single$beta_true)[   c("gic", "TP", "FP", "FN", "TN", "F1_score", "MCC")] L0glm.metrics(single_cv$fit_best, beta_true=single$beta_true)[   c("gic", "TP", "FP", "FN", "TN", "F1_score", "MCC")] # fit_1se is a full-data model, ready for prediction or coefficient extraction. fitted(single_cv$fit_1se)[1:6, , drop=FALSE]  # Grouped multichannel Poisson deconvolution, keeping every channel. multi <- simul(method=4, n=500, p=500, s=.05, seed=2) multi_gic <- L0glm.tune(multi$X, multi$y, family=poisson(identity),   tune="gic", nlambda=5, prop_range=.25, coefs.true=multi$beta_true,   nonnegative=TRUE, grouped=TRUE, relaxed=TRUE, parallelize=FALSE, plot=TRUE)  # All channels of each time point share one fold assignment. folds <- rep(1:3, length.out=nrow(multi$X)) multi_cv <- L0glm.tune(multi$X, multi$y, family=poisson(identity),   tune="cv", nlambda=5, prop_range=.25, nfolds=3, foldid=folds,   coefs.true=multi$beta_true,   nonnegative=TRUE, grouped=TRUE, relaxed=TRUE, parallelize=FALSE, plot=TRUE) c(GIC=multi_gic$lambda_best, CV=multi_cv$lambda_best,   CV_1se=multi_cv$lambda_1se, GIC_preset=multi_cv$lambda_preset) L0glm.metrics(multi_gic$fit_best, beta_true=multi$beta_true)[   c("gic", "TP", "FP", "FN", "TN", "F1_score", "MCC",     "within_row_F1_score", "within_row_MCC")] L0glm.metrics(multi_cv$fit_best, beta_true=multi$beta_true)[   c("gic", "TP", "FP", "FN", "TN", "F1_score", "MCC",     "within_row_F1_score", "within_row_MCC")] dim(coef(multi_cv$fit_1se))            # all original predictor rows and channels  # High-dimensional Gaussian regression with 60 positive/negative effects. # X alone needs about 4 GB; set p <- 20000L for a smaller example. if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ n <- 500L p <- 1000000L set.seed(123) X_hd <- matrix(rnorm(n*p), n, p) support <- sample.int(p, 60L) beta_hd <- numeric(p) beta_hd[support] <- runif(60L, -.8, .8) mean_hd <- as.numeric(X_hd[, support, drop=FALSE] %*% beta_hd[support]) set.seed(1) y_hd <- mean_hd + rnorm(n)  # screen="auto" applies p_eligible > 10*n independently at each lambda, # with n equal to the training row count, including within each CV fold. hd_gic <- L0glm.tune(X_hd, y_hd, family=gaussian(), tune="gic",   nlambda=5, coefs.true=beta_hd, screen.nthreads=8, nthreads=1, plot=FALSE) # Screening and preprocessing are recomputed within each training fold. set.seed(42) hd_cv <- L0glm.tune(X_hd, y_hd, family=gaussian(), tune="cv",   nlambda=5, nfolds=3, coefs.true=beta_hd,   screen.nthreads=8, nthreads=1, plot=FALSE) c(GIC=hd_gic$lambda_best, CV=hd_cv$lambda_best,   CV_1se=hd_cv$lambda_1se, GIC_preset=hd_cv$lambda_preset) hd_cv$metrics[c("lambda", "cv_deviance", "cv_se")] L0glm.metrics(hd_gic$fit_best, beta_true=beta_hd)[   c("gic", "TP", "FP", "FN", "TN", "F1_score", "MCC")] L0glm.metrics(hd_cv$fit_best, beta_true=beta_hd)[   c("gic", "TP", "FP", "FN", "TN", "F1_score", "MCC")] hd_cv$fit_best$screening$history dim(coef(hd_cv$fit_1se))              # screened-out predictors remain zero rows } # }  # CV plots show mean held-out deviance +/- one standard error. Vertical # lines mark lambda_best, lambda_1se and the full-data GIC preset. par(old_par) # Sparse special families: GIC preset fits, GIC tuning and three-fold CV. if (requireNamespace("mgcv", quietly=TRUE)) {   set.seed(204)   n <- 300L   X_special <- matrix(rnorm(n*20), n, 20)   folds_special <- sample(rep(1:3, length.out=n))   family_par <- par(mgp=c(2, .7, 0))    # Negative binomial: two nonzero slopes among 20 predictors.   mu_nb <- exp(.4 + .8*X_special[, 1] - .6*X_special[, 2])   y_nb <- rnbinom(n, mu=mu_nb, size=2)   # nb() estimates theta; nb(theta=2) would keep it fixed at two.   nb_fit <- L0glm.fit(X_special, y_nb, family=mgcv::nb(),     intercept=TRUE, lambda="gic", relaxed=TRUE, maxit=100, tol=1e-8)   nb_fit$theta   coef(nb_fit)   nb_gic <- L0glm.tune(X_special, y_nb, family=mgcv::nb(),     intercept=TRUE, tune="gic", nlambda=5,     relaxed=TRUE, maxit=100, tol=1e-8)   nb_cv <- L0glm.tune(X_special, y_nb, family=mgcv::nb(),     intercept=TRUE, tune="cv", nlambda=5, nfolds=3, foldid=folds_special,     relaxed=TRUE, maxit=100, tol=1e-8)   c(GIC=nb_gic$lambda_best, CV=nb_cv$lambda_best, CV_1se=nb_cv$lambda_1se)   predict(nb_cv$fit_1se, X_special[1:5, , drop=FALSE], type="response")    # Three-category multinomial: only two predictor rows affect probabilities.   eta <- cbind(0, .9*X_special[, 1] - .7*X_special[, 2],     -.8*X_special[, 1] + .6*X_special[, 2])   probabilities <- exp(eta - apply(eta, 1, max))   probabilities <- probabilities/rowSums(probabilities)   y_multinomial <- factor(vapply(seq_len(n), function(i)     sample.int(3, 1, prob=probabilities[i, ]), integer(1)), levels=1:3)   multinomial_fit <- L0glm.fit(X_special, y_multinomial,     family=mgcv::multinom(K=2), lambda="gic", grouped=TRUE,     relaxed=TRUE, maxit=200, tol=1e-8)   coef(multinomial_fit)               # original-scale, zero-sum CLR rows   multinomial_gic <- L0glm.tune(X_special, y_multinomial,     family=mgcv::multinom(K=2), tune="gic", nlambda=5, grouped=TRUE,     relaxed=TRUE, maxit=200, tol=1e-8)   multinomial_cv <- L0glm.tune(X_special, y_multinomial,     family=mgcv::multinom(K=2), tune="cv", nlambda=5,     nfolds=3, foldid=folds_special, grouped=TRUE,     relaxed=TRUE, maxit=200, tol=1e-8)   c(GIC=multinomial_gic$lambda_best, CV=multinomial_cv$lambda_best,     CV_1se=multinomial_cv$lambda_1se)   predict(multinomial_cv$fit_1se, X_special[1:5, , drop=FALSE], type="response")    # Right-censored Cox model: two nonzero log-hazard effects, no intercept.   if (requireNamespace("survival", quietly=TRUE)) {     event_time <- rexp(n, rate=exp(.7*X_special[, 1] - .5*X_special[, 2]))     censor_time <- rexp(n, rate=.4)     y_cox <- survival::Surv(pmin(event_time, censor_time),       event_time <= censor_time)     cox_fit <- L0glm.fit(X_special, y_cox, family=mgcv::cox.ph(),       lambda="gic", relaxed=TRUE, maxit=100, tol=1e-8)     coef(cox_fit)     cox_gic <- L0glm.tune(X_special, y_cox, family=mgcv::cox.ph(),       tune="gic", nlambda=5, relaxed=TRUE, maxit=100, tol=1e-8)     cox_cv <- L0glm.tune(X_special, y_cox, family=mgcv::cox.ph(),       tune="cv", nlambda=5, nfolds=3, foldid=folds_special,       relaxed=TRUE, maxit=100, tol=1e-8)     c(GIC=cox_gic$lambda_best, CV=cox_cv$lambda_best, CV_1se=cox_cv$lambda_1se)     predict(cox_cv$fit_1se, X_special[1:5, , drop=FALSE], type="risk")   }   par(family_par) }

--- true point-spread function (PSF) ----------------------------- L       <- 51                       # kernel length sigma1  <- 1.25                     # left-hand sigma sigma2  <- 5                        # right-hand sigma g_true  <- convkernel("bigaussian", L,                       params = list(sigma1 = sigma1,                                     sigma2 = sigma2),                       perc   = "mean") # match the fitted PSF's centroid convention  ## --- latent sparse spike-train ------------------------------------ n        <- 10000L                  # timepoints npeaks   <- 1000L                   # nonzero peaks idx      <- sample(n, npeaks) amps     <- sample(1000:100000, npeaks) a_true   <- numeric(n);  a_true[idx] <- amps   # true spikes  ## --- baseline ----------------------------------------------------- baseline <- "intercept" # or "bspline" or NULL if (!is.null(baseline)) {if (baseline=="intercept") {   X_baseline <- Matrix::Matrix(1, n, 1, sparse = TRUE)   a_baseline <- 5000 } else if (baseline=="bspline") {   nknots <- max(4L, floor(n/500))   X_baseline <- splines::bs(seq_len(n), df = nknots, degree = 3)   X_baseline <- Matrix::Matrix(X_baseline, sparse = TRUE)   a_baseline <- runif(nknots, min = 2000, max = 6000) }} else { X_baseline <- NULL }  ## --- generate blurred, noisy observations ------------------------- X_sim  <- convmatrix(g_true, n) if (!is.null(X_baseline)) { X_full <- cbind(X_baseline, X_sim) a_full <- c(a_baseline, a_true) y_baseline <- as.vector(X_baseline %*% a_baseline) # noiseless baseline } else {   X_full <- X_sim   a_full <- a_true   y_baseline <- rep(0, n) }  y_true <- as.vector(X_full %*% a_full)    # noiseless convolution y      <- rpois(n, y_true)                # with Poisson noise  # quick sanity plot plot(y, type = "l", ylim = c(0,max(y)),      main = "Simulated blurred spike train with baseline in red") lines(y_baseline, col="red")  ## ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ## 2  Blind deconvolution starting from intial Gaussian PSF guess ## ------------------------------------------------------------------------ g0 <- convkernel("gaussian", L, list(sigma = 6))  # initial guess for PSF  fit <- L0glm_blind_deco(y,                         family = poisson(identity),                         L = L,                 # PSF kernel length                         baseline = baseline,                         kernel_est = g0,                         kernel_smoothfun = function(y) {                           log_conc_smooth(y, nknots = round(L / 5))                         },                         perc = "mean",         # use centroid centering                         kernel_true = g_true,  # for plots                         IC = "gic",                         plot = TRUE,                         tol = 1e-3)  plot(fit$deviance_trace, type="l", log="y",      xlab="Iteration", ylab="Deviance",      main="Poisson L0 glm blind deconvolution\nconvergence behaviour") a_est = as.vector(fit$a_hat)   # estimated spikes g_est = fit$g_hat              # estimated PSF  ## ---------- summary statistics ------------------------------------ n_true <- sum(a_true != 0) n_est  <- sum(a_est  != 0) tp     <- sum(a_true != 0 & a_est != 0) precision <- tp / n_est recall    <- tp / n_true F1        <- 2 * precision * recall / (precision + recall) R2p <- 100 * summary(lm(a_true ~ 0 + a_est))$r.squared  ## ---------- scatter-plot with true vs. estimated peak areas ------- main_expr <- bquote(   atop("Poisson L0 glm blind deconvolution",        atop("true vs. estimated peak areas",             italic(R)^2 == .(sprintf("%.2f", R2p)) * "%" ~ "|" ~               "peaks:" ~ .(n_true) ~ "(true)," ~ .(n_est) ~ "(est.)" ~ "|" ~               "F1 =" ~ .(sprintf("%.2f", 100 * F1)) * "%"))) plot(a_est, a_true,      xlim = range(a_est, a_true),      ylim = range(a_est, a_true),      pch  = 16, col = "blue",      xlab = "estimated value",      ylab = "true value",      main = main_expr)  # Multichannel fits use an individual background offset for each channel. Y <- cbind(y, rpois(n, 0.7 * y_true), rpois(n, 1.3 * y_true)) multi <- L0glm_blind_deco(Y, family = poisson(identity), kernel_est = g0,                          baseline = "bspline", nknots = 6L,                          maxiter = 3L, plot = FALSE) dim(multi$a_hat) multi$deviance  # Estimate smoothly varying PSFs in ten overlapping windows. # The returned X can also be supplied to splogconNMF(). varying <- L0glm_blind_deco(y, family = poisson(identity), kernel_est = g0,                            baseline = "bspline", nknots = 8L,                            nwindows = 10L, maxiter = 6L) dim(varying$g_hat)  # 10 local PSFs dim(varying$X)      # sparse scan-by-scan design # }

title: Sparse deconvolution with a fixed PSF via L0-penalised GLMs — L0glm_sparse_deco
code: ## ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ## 1  Simulate a blurred spike-train with a BIGAUSSIAN PSF & Poisson noise ## ------------------------------------------------------------------------ library(Matrix) library(splines) set.seed(123) family <- poisson(identity)  ## --- true point-spread function (PSF) ----------------------------- L       <- 51                       # kernel length sigma1  <- 1.25                     # left-hand sigma sigma2  <- 5                        # right-hand sigma g_true  <- convkernel("bigaussian", L,                       params = list(sigma1 = sigma1,                                     sigma2 = sigma2),                       perc   = 0)   # already centred  ## --- latent sparse spike-train ------------------------------------ n        <- 500L                    # timepoints npeaks   <- 50L                     # nonzero peaks idx      <- sample(n, npeaks) amps     <- sample(1000:100000, npeaks) a_true   <- numeric(n);  a_true[idx] <- amps   # true spikes  ## --- baseline ----------------------------------------------------- baseline <- "intercept" # or "bspline" or NULL  if (!is.null(baseline)) {if (baseline=="intercept") {   X_baseline <- Matrix::Matrix(1, n, 1, sparse = TRUE)   a_baseline <- 5000 } else if (baseline=="bspline") {   nknots <- max(4L, floor(n/500))   X_baseline <- splines::bs(seq_len(n), df = nknots, degree = 3) X_baseline <- Matrix::Matrix(X_baseline, sparse = TRUE)   a_baseline <- runif(nknots, min = 2000, max = 6000) }} else { X_baseline <- NULL }  ## --- generate blurred, noisy observations ------------------------- X_sim  <- convmatrix(g_true, n) if (!is.null(X_baseline)) { X_full <- cbind(X_baseline, X_sim) a_full <- c(a_baseline, a_true) y_baseline <- as.vector(X_baseline %*% a_baseline) # noiseless baseline   } else {    X_full <- X_sim   a_full <- a_true   y_baseline <- rep(0, n) }  y_true <- as.vector(X_full %*% a_full)    # noiseless convolution y      <- rpois(n, y_true)                # with Poisson noise   # quick sanity plot plot(y, type = "l", ylim = c(0,max(y)), main = "Simulated blurred spike train with baseline in red") lines(y_baseline, col="red")  ## ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ## 2  Deconvolution with the known PSF ## ------------------------------------------------------------------------  fit <- L0glm_sparse_deco(y, kernel = g_true,                          family = poisson(identity),                          baseline = baseline,                           IC = "gic") a_est_baseline <- as.vector(fit$coef_baseline)  a_est <- as.vector(fit$coef_spikes) sum(a_est!=0)   ## ---------- summary statistics ------------------------------------ n_true <- sum(a_true != 0) n_est  <- sum(a_est  != 0) tp     <- sum(a_true != 0 & a_est != 0) precision <- tp / n_est recall    <- tp / n_true F1        <- 2 * precision * recall / (precision + recall) R2p <- 100 *   summary(lm(a_true ~ 0 + a_est))$r.squared R2p  ## ---------- scatter-plot with true vs. estimated peak areas ------- main_expr <- bquote(   atop("Poisson L0-glm deconvolution with known PSF",        atop("true vs. estimated peak areas",             italic(R)^2 == .(sprintf("%.2f", R2p)) * "%" ~ "|" ~               "peaks:" ~ .(n_true) ~ "(true)," ~ .(n_est) ~ "(est.)" ~ "|" ~               "F1 =" ~ .(sprintf("%.2f", 100 * F1)) * "%")))  plot(a_est, a_true,      xlim = range(a_est, a_true),      ylim = range(a_est, a_true),      pch  = 16, col = "blue",      xlab = "estimated value",      ylab = "true value",      main = main_expr)  # Fit several outcome channels jointly, with their own baseline coefficients. Y <- cbind(y, rpois(n, 0.7 * y_true), rpois(n, 1.3 * y_true)) multi <- L0glm_sparse_deco(Y, kernel = g_true, family = poisson(identity),                           baseline = "bspline", nknots = 6L) dim(multi$coef_spikes) dim(multi$coef_baseline)

title: Fast nonnegative identity-link Poisson L0 or grouped L0 penalized fit — L0nnpois
code: ## Fast nonnegative identity-link Poisson L0 or grouped L0 penalized fit ## All coefficients, including an optional intercept, are always nonnegative. ## No nonnegative, lower or upper argument is needed or accepted. n <- p <- 1000 npeaks <- 100  sim.pois.mc <- simul(method = 4, n = n, p = p, s = npeaks / p, seed = 2) dim(sim.pois.mc$beta_true) # 1000 x 176 channels  ## Multichannel fit. OpenMP is used across outcome channels when available. system.time(fit.mc <- L0nnpois(   sim.pois.mc$X,   sim.pois.mc$y,   lambda = "gic",   grouped = TRUE,   relaxed = TRUE,   parallelize = TRUE,   ncores = round(parallel::detectCores(logical = FALSE)/2) ))  # with n <- p <- 1000 and npeaks <- 100   0.56s with 4 cores on my machine # with n <- p <- 10000 and npeaks <- 1000 9.41s with 4 cores on my machine  dim(fit.mc$coefficients) sum(fit.mc$coefficients != 0)  ## A six-coefficient nonnegative spline background, refined on every channel. B <- splines::bs(seq(0, 1, length.out=n), df=6, intercept=TRUE) set.seed(3) alpha <- outer(c(2, 5, 3, 7, 4, 2), rep(1, ncol(sim.pois.mc$y))) Y_background <- sim.pois.mc$y + matrix(rpois(length(sim.pois.mc$y), B %*% alpha),   n, ncol(sim.pois.mc$y)) compulsory <- p + seq_len(ncol(B)) fit_background <- L0nnpois(cbind(sim.pois.mc$X, Matrix::Matrix(B, sparse=TRUE)),   Y_background, always.include=compulsory, lambda="gic", ncores=4L,   precluster=TRUE, control.precluster=list(k.max=32L, rowbins=5L)) background_hat <- B %*% as.matrix(coef(fit_background)[compulsory, , drop=FALSE]) fit_background$nuisance$seconds  if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ ## Compare with the general R fitting path (process-based parallelism): system.time(fit.mc <- L0glm.fit(   X = sim.pois.mc$X,   y = sim.pois.mc$y,   family = poisson(identity),   lambda = "gic",   nonnegative = TRUE,   openmp = FALSE,   grouped = TRUE,   relaxed = TRUE,   parallelize = TRUE,   ncores = round(parallel::detectCores(logical = FALSE)/2) ))  # with n <- p <- 1000 and npeaks <- 100   11.84s with 4 cores on my machine # with n <- p <- 10000 and npeaks <- 1000 38.55s with 4 cores on my machine  dim(fit.mc$coefficients) sum(fit.mc$coefficients != 0) } # }  ## Single-channel fit uses the same nonnegative model. system.time(fit.sc <- L0nnpois(   sim.pois.mc$X,   sim.pois.mc$y[, 1L],   lambda = "gic",   grouped = FALSE,   relaxed = FALSE,   parallelize = FALSE ))  # with n <- p <- 1000 and npeaks <- 100   0.03s on my machine # with n <- p <- 10000 and npeaks <- 1000 0.13s on my machine  sum(fit.sc$coefficients != 0)  ## Native validation stopping with an independent repeat measurement. small <- simul(n = 300L, p = 300L, n_nonzero = 20L, m = 4L, seed = 7L) set.seed(8) y.validation <- matrix(rpois(length(small$y_true), small$y_true), 300L, 4L) validated <- L0nnpois(small$X, small$y, lambda = "gic", ncores = 2L,   validation = list(X = small$X, y = y.validation, patience = 3L)) validated$validation$deviance validated$validation$selection$history  ## Compare with the general R path for a single channel: system.time(fit.sc <- L0glm.fit(   X = sim.pois.mc$X,   y = sim.pois.mc$y[, 1L],   family = poisson(identity),   lambda = "gic",   nonnegative = TRUE,   openmp = FALSE,   grouped = FALSE,   relaxed = FALSE,   parallelize = FALSE ))  # with n <- p <- 1000 and npeaks <- 100   0.04s on my machine # with n <- p <- 10000 and npeaks <- 1000 0.25s on my machine  sum(fit.sc$coefficients != 0)

title: Fits a ridge regularised weighted least squares regression using a chosen solver subject to optional nonnegativity or box constraints on the coefficients. — lmridge
text: lmridge function fits ridge regression model form: $$\beta = \arg \min_{\beta} \left\{ \frac{1}{2} \| W^{1/2}(y - X \beta) \|_2^2 + \frac{1}{2}\sum_j \lambda_j (\beta_j - \mu_j)^2 \right\}$$   \(W\) contains observation weights, \(\lambda_j\) ridge   penalty parameters, \(\mu\) prior mean coefficients   (specified prior.mean). function supports optional bounds coefficients via   lower upper parameters can impose nonnegativity   constraints nonnegative = TRUE. scaling parameter allows scaling predictors. scaling   applied, coefficients rescaled back original scale   returned. Different solvers can specified via solver parameter: "eigen" Uses Eigen package solve ridge   regression problem using one several solvers (see method option). "bigGlm" Uses bigGlm function glmnet package solve ridge regression problem. "glmnet" alias. "osqp" Uses osqp package (Operator Splitting Quadratic Program solver) solve problem constraints. appropriate box nonnegativity constraints applied. method parameter specifies specific method used   "eigen" solver used (1=Cholesky LLT, 2=Cholesky LDLT,   3=CG incomplete Cholesky preconditioning sparse systems   diagonal preconditioning dense systems, 4=LSCG diagonal   least-squares preconditioner, 5=column-pivoted QR, 6=BDCSVD dense   systems Jacobi SVD sparse systems). LSCG uses Eigen's diagonal least-squares preconditioner without additional   external column equilibration. finite approximate LSCG solution   retained warning requested tolerance reached;   missing nonfinite solution triggers Cholesky fallback. OSQP uses   original coefficient coordinates reports warning   requested accuracy reached. failed OSQP setup solve,   infeasible/nonconvex status, invalid returned coefficient vector,   warning issued previous IRLS coefficients (clipped   bounds) retained. warning establish convergence.   Finite-tolerance solutions can change subsequent adaptive ridge   selection path. Eligible wide Eigen ridge systems use Woodbury identity solve   observation-space system dimension n, rather predictor-space   system dimension p. requested Eigen method retained.   LLT, LDLT CG, default forms Gram matrix directly dense   predictors. Sparse predictors, dense-stored working matrices   least one million entries fewer 10 percent nonzeros, use sparse   row augmentation. Set control.solver$rowaug explicitly override   automatic choice.   Dense sparse designs retain storage type; optional row augmentation   constructs sparse augmented matrix. Eigen's SVD requires dense factorization   internally even input sparse. OSQP requires sparse arrays   solver boundary.

code: if (requireNamespace("cobs", quietly = TRUE)) { set.seed(1) x      <- seq(-5, 5, length.out = 101)  ## underlying "true" density on the grid f_true <- dnorm(x) f_true <- f_true / sum(f_true)          # ensure it integrates to 1  N      <- 100000                        # total expected counts lambda <- N * f_true                    # Poisson means in each bin  y_cnt  <- rpois(length(x), lambda)      # Poisson-noisy counts y      <- y_cnt / sum(y_cnt)            # rescale back to a density  g <- log_conc_smooth(y)  matplot(cbind(y, f_true, g), type = "l", lty = 1,         col = c(2, 1, 4), ylab = "density",         main = "Raw (Poisson) vs. log-concave smoothed curve + ground truth") legend("topleft", legend = c("raw (Poisson)", "smoothed", "ground truth"),        col = c(2, 4, 1), lty = 1, bty = "n") }

title: Simulate sparse GLMs and deconvolution problems — simul
code: # Blurred spike trains with a known PSF, sparse peaks and an optional baseline. single <- simul("deconvolution", n=200, p=200, n_nonzero=20,   family="poisson", intercept=1, seed=2) multi <- simul("deconvolution", n=100, p=120, n_nonzero=10,   family="gaussian", m=4, intercept=c(1, 2, 3, 4), seed=2,   options=list(mean_beta=100, sd_noise=2)) dim(multi$beta_true)                  # 120 slopes plus an intercept, four channels if (requireNamespace("mgcv", quietly=TRUE)) {   nb_spikes <- simul("deconvolution", n=100, p=100, n_nonzero=10,     family="nb", m=4, intercept=1, options=list(theta=5)) }  # Standard normal predictors, arbitrary n/p, and signed sparse coefficients. regression <- simul("normal", n=150, p=30, n_nonzero=4, intercept=1.5,   options=list(beta_range=c(-2, 2), error_sd=.5), seed=10) fit <- L0glm.fit(regression$X, regression$y, family=regression$family,   intercept=regression$intercept, nonnegative=FALSE, parallelize=FALSE) L0glm.metrics(fit, beta_true=regression$beta_true)[c("gic", "F1_score", "MCC")]  # sparseglm reads family, intercept and coefficient truth from the simulation. comparison <- sparseglm(regression, method=c("L0glm", "lasso"), nlambda=5) L0glm.metrics(comparison)[c("method", "seconds", "gic", "F1_score", "MCC")]  # ABESS-style correlated predictors and coefficient magnitudes. abess_data <- simul("abess", n=200, p=100, n_nonzero=5,   family="binomial", intercept=-1, options=list(cortype=2, rho=.5))  # Best-subset pattern 3: decreasing effects, population SNR=2, validation data. subset_data <- simul("bestsubset", n=100, p=50, n_nonzero=5, intercept=2,   options=list(beta.type=3, rho=.5, snr=2, nval=50)) subset_data$dispersion dim(subset_data$Xval)  # Other standard links and special families use the same normal-design setup. probit_data <- simul("normal", n=100, p=20, n_nonzero=3,   family=binomial("probit"), intercept=-.5) gamma_data <- simul("normal", n=100, p=20, n_nonzero=3,   family=Gamma("log"), intercept=1, options=list(dispersion=.5)) if (requireNamespace("mgcv", quietly=TRUE) && requireNamespace("survival", quietly=TRUE)) {   nb_data <- simul("normal", n=150, p=20, n_nonzero=3,     family=mgcv::nb(), intercept=1, options=list(theta=3))   multinomial_data <- simul("normal", n=150, p=20, n_nonzero=3,     family=mgcv::multinom(K=2), intercept=c(.3, 0, -.3))   cox_data <- simul("normal", n=150, p=20, n_nonzero=3,     family=mgcv::cox.ph(), intercept=log(2)) # doubles the baseline hazard   cox_data$intercept                    # FALSE: no estimable Cox intercept }

code: set.seed(1) n <- 150; p <- 300 X <- matrix(rnorm(n*p),n,p) beta <- c(1,-1,.8,-.8,rep(0,p-4)) y <- as.numeric(X%*%beta)+rnorm(n) screen <- sis_glm(X,y,nsis=40,return_stats=FALSE) screen$indices threaded <- sis_glm(X,y,nsis=40,return_stats=FALSE,nthreads=4) identical(threaded$indices,screen$indices)  # Independent channels are screened jointly without signed cancellation. multi <- sis_glm(X,cbind(y,-y),nsis=40,return_stats=FALSE) multi$indices  # Conditional screening includes the specified nuisance design. conditional <- sis_glm(X,y,nuisance=cbind(1,X[,1]),nsis=40) head(conditional$stats[conditional$ranking,])  # Offset-based outer ISIS; each candidate fit starts afresh. iterated <- sis_glm(X,y,nsis=40,iterative=TRUE,niter=10,return_stats=FALSE) iterated$history coef(iterated$fit)                 # sparse, all original predictor rows head(predict(iterated$fit,X[1:5,,drop=FALSE]))  # The same full-dimension model through the main fitting interface. fit <- L0glm.fit(X,y,screen="ISIS",nsis=40,screen.maxit=10,screen.nthreads=4) fit$screening$history coef(fit) # screen="auto" (the default) enables ISIS exactly when p_eligible > 10*n. # Use screen="none" to fit the full design directly.  if (requireNamespace("mgcv",quietly=TRUE)) {   counts <- rnbinom(n,mu=exp(.5+.4*X[,1]),size=2)   nb <- sis_glm(X,counts,family=mgcv::nb(),nsis=20,return_stats=FALSE)   nb$theta   classes <- factor(sample(letters[1:3],n,TRUE))   multinomial <- sis_glm(X,classes,family=mgcv::multinom(2),                         nsis=20,return_stats=FALSE) } if (requireNamespace("mgcv",quietly=TRUE) && requireNamespace("survival",quietly=TRUE)) {   time <- rexp(n,exp(.5*X[,1]))   outcome <- survival::Surv(pmin(time,2),time<=2)   cox <- sis_glm(Matrix::Matrix(X,sparse=TRUE),outcome,                 family=mgcv::cox.ph(),nsis=20,return_stats=FALSE) }

code: # Sparse Gaussian regression. set.seed(1) X <- matrix(rnorm(360),60,6) truth <- c(2,-1,rep(0,4)) y <- as.numeric(X %*% truth + rnorm(60)) comparison <- sparseglm(X,y,method=c("lasso","relaxed_lasso"),   tune="gic",nlambda=5,beta_true=truth) L0glm.metrics(comparison)[c("method","seconds","gic","adj_R2_weighted","F1_score","MCC")] plot(comparison,which=c(1,2))  # Blurred Poisson spike trains: smaller versions of the single/multichannel # deconvolution benchmarks. code: set.seed(12) n <- 300L psf <- convkernel("gaussian", 21L, list(sigma = 2)) X <- convmatrix(psf, n) H <- cbind(X[, c(45, 95, 160, 235)],            pmax(0, 1 - abs(seq_len(n) - 185) / 22)) H <- H %*% Matrix::Diagonal(x = 1 / Matrix::colSums(H)) S <- matrix(rexp(5 * 8, rate = 1 / 3000), 5, 8) B <- splines::bs(seq_len(n), df = 4, intercept = TRUE) mu <- as.matrix(H %*% S) + B %*% matrix(20, 4, 8) Y <- matrix(rpois(length(mu), mu), n, 8) fit <- splogconNMF(X, Y, background = B, family = poisson("identity"),   precluster = 4L, correlation = "none", ncores = 2L) fit c(compounds = fit$rank, GIC = GIC(fit), seconds = fit$seconds[["total"]]) matplot(fit$H, type = "l", lty = 1, xlab = "Scan", ylab = "Elution profile")  # For overdispersed intensities, estimate one common noise scale from temporal # differences. Selection and fusion use four groups; the result has all channels. Yq <- 5 * matrix(rpois(length(mu), mu / 5), n, 8) fitq <- splogconNMF(X, Yq, background = B, family = quasipoisson("identity"),   precluster = 4L, correlation = "none", ncores = 2L) GIC(fitq)  # Other identity-link choices include gaussian(), mgcv::nb(), Gamma(), # nb1(dispersion=5, link="identity"), and # Gamma_scale(scale=5, link="identity", censor=0.5).
